title: Night Baron Murder Case
subtitle_source: case_closed_dataset/subs_resolved/0068.txt, case_closed_dataset/subs_resolved/0070.txt (middle episode 0069 transcript was not part of this batch, so the middle-episode dialogue is reconstructed only from what 0068 sets up and 0070 recaps/resolves)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, an unnamed knocked-out police officer) omitted by convention; their off-screen involvement (Conan pushed into the pool, Kogoro drugged and publicly misfiring his deduction at Maeda, the officer knocked out) is preserved instead as attrs on the relevant object/person nodes so the facts aren't lost. No event nodes: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved, sharing an order integer. Two Night Baron costumes are modeled as separate object instances since they are physically distinct props used by two different people for two different purposes. The strongest red herring is Satoru Maeda, who genuinely did commit a second, real act (stealing a spare costume and staging a fight to mislead investigators) after independently suspecting his fiancee, making Kogoro's public accusation against him wrong about the murder but not baseless about his behavior. Konno and Kamijo are also treated with suspicion (unverified alibi / drugging behavior) before being cleared. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The second Night Baron sighting required knocking out a third-dan black-belt officer in a single blow and evading Ran's kicks entirely -- only the former karate champion Maeda could plausibly do this. This genuinely implicates him in staging that later appearance, but not in the murder itself, since he has an independent alibi for the time Ebara actually died.

Test blankets dressed as decoys and dropped from every suspect's room show that, given the Princess Wind blowing across the courtyard that night, only a drop from the one room sheltered from the wind -- Sayama's, directly below Ebara's balcony -- lands where Ebara's body actually did; every other room's decoy, including Ebara's own, is blown well off to the side.

Cellophane tape residue is found in the blind spot of Ebara's room's security lock -- proof the lock was set from outside the room after the killer already had his key, meaning the room was staged to look like the murder scene before the body was ever moved there.
